title: Her first records: OKeh, Brunswick and the Spencer Williams songs
summary: Allen asks who accompanied her records. She recalls an OKeh studio band, pianist Clarence Johnson, and Russell Robinson on the Brunswick sides.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you a few questions about your phonograph record. I know this is going to be kind of hard on your memory. But do you remember who you made Grieving Mama Blues and Slow Up Papa with? Oh, that's on the OK. With Piana and Cornette.

On the OK? With Piana and Cornette? Yeah. Well... No, I can't remember because... Well, I mean, you see, by not having my own accompaniment, I had to just sing with anybody that they would just get, you know? And they just would... Every time I went there, there was somebody different, you know? But I don't remember who that cornette player or piano player was. But did you look on the record? They usually put the name on the record. No, it's not on that record. No. Slow Up Papa.
Slow Up Papa. What about those OKs?

Well, the OK records, you see, those were the first records that I made, and it was with a white band there that played by music. They didn't play by like that, no Dixieland, no jazz, nothing like that. They strictly played music. And most of their arrangements was made for them by Bob Rickards. So I don't remember the names of the musicians, either. You know?
Yeah. What about this fellow, Clarence Johnson?
Well, he was from Chicago. He was quite a piano player. Yes, he was quite a piano player. And I did quite a few records with him.
You know, I looked through here and I didn't find any list in here of Russell Robinson on Brunswick with you. You say you made a record with him?
That's right. I made the Haitian blues. Haitian blues, I think, and Black Man Be On Your Way. On the Brunswick.
They got that as Clarence Johnson and Spencer Williams.
I mean, the writers who wrote the piece. They wrote the piece.

They're the writers of the piece. Clarence Williams is, I mean, Spencer Williams is the writer of the Haitian blues. See? But Russell Robinson is the one who played the piano. And you played the gazook. And I played the gazook. That's right.
